title: Why does Mira's puzzle always end in the same number?
description: Sanju and Mira are on a train. The video follows Mira's steps for the digits three and seven and shows why each answer is nine times the gap between the digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: tens are nine more than ones, so each answer is nine times the gap between the digits. Watch for children who think the numbers are as far apart as the digits.

source: Follow Mira's steps for the digits 3 and 7 and say why each
video_script.why: The child can follow the steps but has not yet seen why every answer is in the table of nine.
video_script.substitution: Split each number into tens and ones; four tens take away four ones is four nines.
video_script.anchor: Sanju and Mira on a train, with Mira's digits written on a card
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says the numbers are four apart, like the digits, but 73 − 37 = 36.
video_script.payoff_line: every answer is nine times the gap between the digits

final_answer.value: 73 − 37 = 36, 63 − 36 = 27, 72 − 27 = 45 and 54 − 45 = 9; every answer is 9 times the gap between the digits
final_answer.spoken: every answer is nine times the gap between the digits

maths_rules: slip: the numbers are not 4 apart; 73 − 37 = 36, not 4
your turn: digits 1 and 9, 91 − 19 = 72 = 9 × 8, the gap 9 − 1 = 8; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: a ten is nine more than a one, so the answer is nine times the gap. Wrong idea: numbers differ as the digits do. The chain of take-aways stays on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='train'/>Sanju and Mira are on a train, and Mira has a number puzzle.
<bookmark mark='make'/>She picks the digits three and seven, and makes thirty seven and seventy three.
<bookmark mark='take'/>She keeps taking away, and every answer sits in the table of nine.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Why does every answer land in the table of nine?

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Take away thirty seven from seventy three, and that makes thirty six.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Use the digits three and six, and sixty three take away thirty six makes twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>Use two and seven, and seventy two take away twenty seven makes forty five.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>Use four and five, and fifty four take away forty five makes nine.
<bookmark mark='s5'/>The answers are thirty six, twenty seven, forty five and nine.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The numbers are four apart, exactly like the digits seven and three.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check it, because seventy three take away thirty seven is thirty six.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Thirty six is far more than four, so the numbers are not that close.

beats.on_screen: 73 is split into 70 and 3; 37 is split into 30 and 7; 70 − 30 = 40 appears; the ones fall 4 short; 40 − 4 = 36 appears; four tens take away four ones is 4 × 10 − 4 × 1 = 4 × 9 = 36

marks.split: 73 is split into 70 and 3; 37 is split into 30 and 7
marks.nines: four tens take away four ones is 4 × 10 − 4 × 1 = 4 × 9 = 36

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Seventy three is seventy and three. Thirty seven is thirty and seven.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Seventy take away thirty leaves forty. The ones fall four short, since three is less than seven.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Forty take away four leaves thirty six in the end.
<bookmark mark='nines'/>That is four tens take away four ones. Ten take away one is nine, so it is four nines.

beats.on_screen: the gap 7 − 3 = 4 is marked beside 36 = 9 × 4; 63 − 36 = 27 = 9 × 3, with the gap 6 − 3 = 3; 72 − 27 = 45 = 9 × 5, with the gap 7 − 2 = 5; 54 − 45 = 9 = 9 × 1, with the gap 5 − 4 = 1; the answer card reads every answer is 9 times the gap between the digits

marks.pay: the answer card reads every answer is 9 times the gap between the digits

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Four is the gap between seven and three, and thirty six is nine fours.
<bookmark mark='r2'/>Sixty three take away thirty six is twenty seven, which is nine times three. The gap between six and three is three.
<bookmark mark='r3'/>Seventy two take away twenty seven is forty five, which is nine times five. The gap between seven and two is five.
<bookmark mark='r4'/>Fifty four take away forty five is nine, which is nine times one. The gap between five and four is one.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Every answer is nine times the gap between the digits.
